text:
carmen: FYI escalation from Acme — customer saw a bunch of 500s and huge tail latency on /v1/generate at ~2024-04-03T18:22Z. They gave this request id: req_9a2f0b4c. Can someone pull server-side slice for that req id? :eyes:

mira: I can take a look, do we have the account/org id and the exact target route + method? also, roughly what region?

carmen: Org ID: org_82x. Route: POST /v1/generate. Region: us-east-1. Customer says spike lasted ~18:22:00-18:24:30 UTC.

jeff: quick note: our ELK retention for logs-prod indices is 14 days by default. If the event is older than that it may be archived to s3-logs. Looks recent so should be in daily index.

mira: running a KQL filter now. Sample query for Kibana: ```kql
index: logs-prod-* AND request_id: "req_9a2f0b4c" OR http.request.id: "req_9a2f0b4c" | sort @timestamp desc```

mira: also try matching on tracing fields: `trace.id: "9a2f0b4c"` and `span.attrs.request_id: "req_9a2f0b4c"` — some services use different field names.

jeff: found lines in logs-prod-2024.04.03, shards 2/2. Looks like a downstream timeout to model-proxy at 18:22:14. Error snippet: ```error="upstream timeout" svc=model-proxy backend=10.2.34.12:8080 duration_ms=12005 request_id=req_9a2f0b4c```

ops_ingrid: tagging @carmen — we have full request lifecycle traces in traces-prod for that trace id. If you want a debug bundle for handoff to eng-runtime, run the internal collector: `./tools/collect-debug --req req_9a2f0b4c --out /tmp/debug-req_9a2f0b4c.tar.gz` then attach to the ticket.

carmen: perfect. Customer also asked for a curl they can run to repro the high latency from their side — what's the minimal curl we should share?

alex: give them the same payload + headers we log: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "X-Request-ID: req_9a2f0b4c" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` — that will reproduce the request path, but not the downstream model backend load.

mira: also include a suggestion to add `X-Debug: capture` header if they can — that routes to a limited debug mode we can correlate with logs when they run it. Example: ```bash
curl -H "X-Debug: capture" -H "X-Request-ID: req_9a2f0b4c" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

carmen: does anyone have a quick KQL to pull the 30s window around the timestamp? I'll paste to the ticket.

jeff: use a range on @timestamp: `@timestamp >= "2024-04-03T18:21:50Z" AND @timestamp <= "2024-04-03T18:24:50Z"` plus the request_id filter. Full KQL: ```kql
index: logs-prod-* AND @timestamp:["2024-04-03T18:21:50Z" TO "2024-04-03T18:24:50Z"] AND (request_id: "req_9a2f0b4c" OR http.request.id: "req_9a2f0b4c")
```

mira: FYI if Kibana doesn't show hits, try the archived buckets: s3://redwood-logs-archive/prod/2024/04/03/ — we have a small lambda that can restore the day's partition. Ping infra if you need restore access.

sre-bot: [automated] Log retention policy: logs-prod-* indices retained 14 days, archived to s3 after rollover. Contact #eng-infra for emergency restore.

carmen: adding to ticket: KQL snippet, curl repro, and internal debug bundle steps. Marking as P1 for now, want eng-runtime to triage the model-proxy timeout.

alex: tagging eng-runtime on the ticket and include this debug bundle when ready. :thumbsup:

mira: I grabbed a 10MB slice with those filters and uploaded to the ticket. If eng-runtime wants raw lines I can export full gzip.

carmen: thanks everyone. If infra needs anything from the customer we'll ask them to run the curl with X-Debug header and send the resulting request id. Closing coordination here. :white_check_mark:
